h1: Pipe sanders and pipe polishing machines
intro: A pipe sander (pipe polisher, tube polishing machine) runs abrasive belts around a round pipe or square tube to grind off rust and weld discolouration, give stainless a satin or brushed finish and prepare tube for painting or plating. The Şahinler BT 114-S is the automatic version: a separate feed motor pushes the tube through two 37 × 2″ belts at an inverter-set speed, so the operator loads the pipe and takes the finished length off the other side without turning or holding it — straight tube and bends up to 45°, Ø3/8″ to Ø4-1/2″. The belt speed is variable too, belts change through an opening cover and a holder is provided for manual feeding. Supplied with two belts, a CSA-approved panel and support from Mississauga, ON.
hero_points: Round pipe and square tube Ø3/8″ to Ø4-1/2″ (10 – 114 mm), straight or bent to 45°

faq.q: What finish does a belt pipe sander give?
faq.a: The finish follows the belt: a coarse grit removes rust, scale and weld colour; 180 – 240 grit gives the brushed, satin finish of architectural stainless handrail; finer belts and non-woven belts prepare for mirror polishing. Two belts run at once on the BT 114-S, so a cutting belt and a finishing belt can be fitted together.

Yes — the belt head and feeder follow bends up to 45°, so handrail elbows and furniture frames are finished after bending instead of before. Tight 90° elbows are finished on the straight sections and blended by hand.

faq.q: Round and square tube on the same machine?
faq.a: Yes. Round pipe from Ø3/8″ to Ø4-1/2″ is clamped by the manual adjustment and fed through; square tube is passed through flat side by side, two faces at a time. The feeder means the operator never turns the material by hand.

faq.q: What about centreless and planetary polishers?
faq.a: For long runs of straight stainless tube to a mirror finish a centreless polisher with several heads is the production machine; for a fabrication shop that finishes handrail, furniture and short lengths in mixed sizes the belt sander with feeder is faster to set up and a fraction of the price. Ask us about both.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
